132's தாமுளராக் கேடின்றால், 'does not perish while they live', is a floor, not a limit. It does not deny 398's எழுமையும் ஏமாப்பு, and 132 itself reaches to எம்மை யுலகத்தும். The supposed qualification depends on reading 'while they live' as 'only while they live', and the note never says which verse limits which.
Both name சோர்வு in speech as the thing to guard against: 642 has காத்தோம்பல் சொல்லின்கட் சோர்வு, and 256 has சொல்லார்தம் சோர்வஞ்சி. 256 shows the learned guarding against it by restraint.
Both open with நீரல்ல சொல்லியக்கால் from those beneath one (நேரல்லார் / நிகரல்லார்). 64 has the excellent not growing angry, and 72 adds that the world counts the opposite as சமழ்மை.

125 says பணிதல் is good for all (எல்லார்க்கும்) and an extra wealth for the rich. 242 makes அடக்கம் the அணிகலம் of the நல்கூர்ந்த மக்கள். That applies the Kural's general claim to the opposite case rather than limiting it.

The clash of images is real: 1113's முத்தம் முறுவல் is exactly what 45 mocks as the chatter of கல்லாப்புன் மாக்கள். But 1113 is dramatised lover's praise (Parimelazhagar calls it புனைந்துரை) and makes no claim that such praise is true or wise, so the incompatibility is thin.
links.text_issue: Naladiyar 45 ends with a stray digit (வேன3).

links.reason: 226 makes relieving அற்றார் அழிபசி the place to store wealth. 170 says செல்வமுடையாருஞ் செல்வரே தற்சேர்ந்தார் அல்லல் களைபவெனின். Both make wealth real only in relieving distress.

153's வன்மையுள் வன்மை மடவார்ப் பொறை is enacted in 155: the good (நல்லார்) listen to a கல்லா ஒருவன், வருந்தியும், to spare him shame. 155 grounds it in kindly regard (கண்ணோடி), but the forbearance toward the ignorant is the same.
links.text_issue: Kural 153 reads இன்நம்யுள் for இன்மையுள் (typo).

links.reason: 951 says செப்பமும் நாணும் exist இயல்பாக only in இற்பிறந்தார். 195 says நல்ல குலம் / தீய குலம் are சொல்லளவு with no substance, and that குலம் is made by தவம் கல்வி ஆள்வினை. The two answer oppositely on whether birth carries moral qualities, and the note names the reconciling reading.

Both list what the fool's life lacks: 327 has இன்புறார், நன்றாற்றார், நன்னெறியும் சேர்கலார், and 338 has அறஞ்செய்யார், ஈகலார், தோள் சேரார், இசைபட வாழார். The note's account of what 338 adds is accurate.
344's தினையனைத்தே ... பனையனைத்தா உள்ளுவர் சான்றோர் restates 104's தினைத்துணை நன்றி ... பனைத்துணையாக் கொள்வர். Mudaliar cites the Kural there, and 344 adds the ungrateful counter-case.
336's நெருநல் உளனொருவன் இன்றில்லை is compressed in 29 to நின்றான் இருந்தான் கிடந்தான் ... சென்றான், which yields இன்னினியே செய்க அறவினை. It is the same claim about how sudden death is.
205's இலன் என்று தீயவை செய்யற்க and 80's தான்கெடினும் தக்கார்கேடெண்ணற்க both forbid letting one's own ruin or poverty excuse doing harm.

27's wise see the body as a rain bubble and resolve தடுமாற்றம் தீர்ப்பேம், which Mudaliar glosses as பிறவித் தடுமாற்றம். 349 says births are cut when attachment ends, and otherwise நிலையாமை is what is seen. Both join seeing impermanence to ending the round of births.
155's ஒறுத்தாரை ஒன்றாக வையாரே ... பொறுத்தாரைப் பொன்போற் பொதிந்து and 72's ஞாலம் treating non-forbearance as சமழ்மை not புகழ்மை both make others' regard the measure of forbearance.

The structures match: 270's ஓதியும் ஓதார் உணர்விலார் and 140's பலகற்றும் கல்லார் அறிவிலாதார். Both say study without understanding or right conduct is not learning, and the note's gloss of the Kural's criterion as conduct in accord with the world is fair.

The vocabulary is shared: பழமை/பழகிய நட்பு and கிழமை/கெழுதகைமை. Both say old intimacy must honour the friend's claim. On Shanmuganar's reading, 310's பொத்தித்தம் நெஞ்சத் தறாஅச் சுடுவதோர் தீ is the cost of refusing it, as the note specifies.

The shared words இன்னர்/இனையர் carry different claims. 790 says friendship cheapens when friends advertise their mutual closeness (புனையினும் புல்லென்னும்). 205 says the great do not sort people into எமர்/பிறர் and help anyone in distress. They do not make the same claim, and 'both distrust speech that labels a relation' stretches the word overlap.

Both teach forbearance through an image from cultivated land: 151's அகழ்வாரைத் தாங்கும் நிலம், and 222's farmers who மறுத்தும் சிறைசெய்வர் when the stream breaks the dam. 222 limits it to தாம்வேண்டிக் கொண்டார் தொடர்பு, chosen friends, but the claim agrees.

195 calls good and bad caste சொல்லளவு and makes worth come from தவம் கல்வி ஆள்வினை. 243 says the same about region: தென்னாட்டவரும் சுவர்க்கம் புகுதலால் தன்னாற்றா னாகும் மறுமை. It is the same claim in a new domain.

Both picture good speech to the unfit as a sweet substance wasted in a filthy place: 720's அங்கணத்துள் உக்க அமிழ்து, and 257's பன்றிக்கூழ்ப் பத்தரில் தேமா வடித்தற்று. The image is distinctive and shared.
Both use the funeral drum: 6's தண்ணம் may sound tomorrow, and 23's மணப்பறை turns into பிணப்பறை in the same hall that day; the shared drum carries the same lesson of sudden death.

Both list three marks of the well-born (சான்றாண்மை சாயல் ஒழுக்கம் / ஒழுக்கமும் வாய்மையும் நாணும் இம்மூன்றும்), and 142 adds that great wealth (பெருஞ்செல்வம் எய்தியக் கண்ணும்) does not give them to others; the note is accurate.

343's worthy keep one course (பெற்றி பிழையாது ஒருநடையர்) even with பெருநடை, and on Pope/Shanmuganar the base keep their low course; 973 says மேலிருந்தும் மேலல்லார் மேலல்லர். Same claim about station not changing nature.
425's மலர்தலும் கூம்பலும் இல்லது is glossed by Parimelazhagar with exactly 215's contrast of கயப்பூ and கோட்டுப்பூ; the opening/closing flower as inconstant friendship is a real shared figure.
5's பின்னாவது என்று பிடித்திரா and 36's அன்றறிவாம் என்னாது both reject deferring virtue, and both tie it to death (கூற்றம் ... சுரம் / பொன்றுங்கால் பொன்றாத் துணை).

333 says act at once on wealth because it does not stay (அற்குப ஆங்கே செயல்); 329 shows the small-minded thinking of மறுமை only in poverty or illness and not when able (ஆற்றிய காலத்து). The negative example confirms the precept.

Both target failing to do what can be done (ஒல்லும் கருமம் உடற்று- / செய்வதனைச் செய்யாது தாழ்த்து) in the setting of false friendship; 818 says drop such friends, 235 that the conduct brings suffering. Close enough to count as agreement.
272's பின்னறிதும் என்பார் are exactly the people 36's அன்றறிவாம் என்னாது warns against; both condemn putting off giving or virtue.
785 says புணர்ச்சி பழகுதல் வேண்டா, feeling alone gives friendship; 154's worthy treat one meeting on the road (ஒருநாள் காணினும்) as தொல்வழிக் கேண்மை. Same claim.
links.text_issue: The Parimelazhagar text shown under 785 (நட்டல் நகுதற்பொருட்டன்று) is the commentary on 784, not 785.

links.reason: Mudaliar does read வற்றாம் ஒருநடை as the base becoming able in a course different from before, which matches 977's இறப்பே புரிந்த; but Pope and Shanmuganar read the base as unchanged, so the link rests on one commentator's gloss of an obscure phrase.
75 lets one bear a friend's conduct ஆற்றும் துணையும் and then withdraw (தூற்றாதே தூர விடல்); 221 says only அடக்கிக் கொளல்வேண்டும். 75 adds a limit to 221's counsel, as the note says.
Both say the base give only under force: 1077's ஈர்ங்கை விதிரார் except to கொடிறுடைக்கும் கூன்கையர், and 355's chisel (உளிநீரார்) that does not cut unless struck, doing all for இன்னாங்கு செய்வார்.

879 says to cut the thorn tree இளைதாக; 241 says the worthy do not advance on a humbled foe, as the snake spares the moon when இளம்பிறை. If 879's tree is an enemy, as the chapter and Parimelazhagar have it, the advice about striking the young or weak foe conflicts; the note names this reading.

Both are the dupe recalling a vow of inseparability (செங்கோடு பாய்துமே / பிரியலம் என்றுரைத்த) that the woman broke; 372 ties it to having no காணம், and 376's money motive is implied by the chapter rather than stated.

52 mocks those who endlessly prattle (பிதற்றும்) of சத்தம் and astrology instead of doing their real work, not lifelong study as such; the limit it puts on 397's praise of learning is real but thinner than the note's 'lifelong study ... madness' suggests.

229 ranks begging above eating alone (இரத்தலின் இன்னாது ... தமியர் உணல்); 288 ranks begging far away (கைந்நீட்டும் கெட்டாற்று வாழ்க்கையே நன்று) above staying home unable to give. Both put a non-giving life below begging; the note marks the different cases.

405's unlearned man's standing wilts when he speaks in company (சொல்லாடச் சோர்வு படும்); 253's man who scorned learning is exposed when a written leaf is held out before many (பல்லார்முன்). Same exposure of the unlearned in public.
108's people who are அறியாரும் அல்லர் yet do பழியோடு பட்டவை, traced to செய்த வினை, are 834's learned man who does not restrain himself; 108 adds a cause while still calling the acts blameworthy.
The verses share ஒப்புரவிற்கு ஒல்கார் almost verbatim, both in poverty (செல்லாமை ... நிற்பினும் / இடனில் பருவத்தும்); 148 adds the eclipsed moon.
117's தம்மை இகழ்வாரைத் ... இகழ்க flatly opposes 151's தம்மை இகழ்வார்ப் பொறுத்தல் தலை on the same situation, the same word இகழ்; the note correctly says it depends on taking 117 as advice.

238's offering one's own life (என் ஆருயிரை ... கைநீட்டேனேல்) under self-curse goes beyond 787's sharing the suffering (அல்லல் உழப்பது); the note itself says it 'raises the stake', which is development, not the same claim.
51's நல்வினை தீர்விடத்து evil returns and 93's wealth leaves when வினையுலந்தக்கால்: 93 applies 51's principle, that good fortune lasts only as long as the merit behind it, to wealth.

11's wise renounce in childhood (குழவி யிடத்தே துறந்தார்) while 46 asks what one gains by going புறத்தாறு if household life is lived by virtue; on the ascetic reading of புறத்தாறு, which the note names, the claims conflict.
521 says only kin keep பழைமை when a man has lost all; 201 shows what seeing உசாஅத்தன் கேளிர் does to the sufferer, like a mother forgetting birth pains. A real development.
Both describe the hoarder who neither enjoys nor uses his store and dies (வைத்துக் கழியும் / வைத்தான் ... அஃதுண்ணான் செத்தான்); 1001 says nothing was achieved, 273 that his wealth laughs at him.

959's கால் (sprout) shows the soil as speech shows lineage, and 367's முளை of red paddy grows true as a son's mind follows his father's; the sprout as evidence of origin is a meaningful shared figure, and the note marks the different logic.
74's அஞ்சுவ தஞ்சி repeats 428's அஞ்சுவது அஞ்சல் அறிவார் தொழில; 74 makes it one of the marks of those who live free of suffering.

212 says a mind cannot be known (மனமறியப் பட்டதொன் றன்று), so trust family (இற்பிறப்பு); 245 says people are as their minds, not their இனம். The note fairly says the conflict depends on இனம் including family.

320 asks whether those without இற்பிறப்பு, however much they learn (எனைத்துநூல் கற்பினும்), can guard others' speech; 409 says the learned born low have worth the unlearned born high lack. The note names the reading the conflict over birth and learning depends on.

On Pope's reading of 223, never saying இலன் and giving marks the well-born; 111 says saying இல் about what one cannot give is வசையன்று, and that the fault lies in false promising. A real limit, though Parimelazhagar reads 223's இலன் as the beggar's own plea.
141's lion that will not eat grass even in இடுக்கண் and 969's கவரிமா that won't live without its hair both stand for the noble who will not drop their principles or honour in extremity.
797 calls leaving fools' friendship ஊதியம்; 239 calls leaving the discerning (நயமுணர்வார் நண்பு) for the புல்லறிவினார் like swapping ghee for neem oil. The reverse exchange confirms the same claim.

179's chapter is நல்லினம் சேர்தல் and its second half speaks of தீயினம், so Mudaliar's reading of குலம் as one's company fits the verse best; the tension depends on Shanmuganar's birth-family reading, which the note names, so it holds only on the weaker reading.
158's three restraints include புறங்கூற்றின் மூகை and end அறங்கூற வேண்டா, echoing 181's அறங்கூறான் ... புறங்கூறான் என்றல் இனிது; both give the abstention from backbiting near-sufficient weight.

The claim of bearing slights without anger is shared, but the note misplaces the figure: 151's earth is the one who bears, while 61's fly (ஈயும் தலைமேல்) is the trivial offender one does not get angry at, not a model of bearing.
656 forbids சான்றோர் பழிக்கும் வினை even to feed one's starving mother; 79 puts பழியாகா ஆறே தலை even above pleasure that would never end. Both set blamelessness above the strongest pull.

48 extends the corpse (முடைச்சாகாடு torn by vultures) to every adorned body, and 913 has the prostitute's embrace as a corpse in the dark; as the note says, this widens the image rather than limiting or conditioning it.
403 says the unlearned are good if they stay silent (சொல்லாதிருக்கப் பெறின்); 155 takes the case where one speaks, and the good listen கண்ணோடி to spare him shame. 155 adds a condition on the learned.

335 says to do good before the hiccup stops the tongue; 183 says to sow seed for மறுமை now because the body changes colour without cause (காரணம் இன்றி). Both urge good deeds now because the body may fail without warning.
184 allows கண்ணின்று கண்ணறச் சொல்லினும் but forbids backbiting; 353 condemns those who proclaim a man's faults உழைநின்று, standing by him, so face-to-face fault-finding is not let off.
links.text_issue: 353 line 2 reads கா஢தால் for அரிதால் (an encoding corruption).

links.reason: 978's சிறுமை அணியுமாம் தன்னை வியந்து is given voice in 165's எம்போல்வார் இல் which 165 denies the name கோள். Same claim.

Both set desire against fire: 1159 says fire burns only தொடின் while love burns விடின், 90 that fire is escaped in water but காமம் சுடும் even under water. A distinctive shared figure in two contexts, adultery and separation.

Both wives see the courtesans' traces on his chest (நீராடாது ... வரைமார்பன் / முலைபொருத தண்சாந் தணியகலம்), but they are sister quatrains in one chapter making one complaint; what links them is the shared image, not a claim that pairing illuminates.

Both use the same formula, அனையம் ... ஊரற்கு அதனால் ... அனையார்க்கு உரை, with a பாண addressee and a neglected side of an object (துடியின் இடக்கண் / கரும்பின் கடைக்கண்); the shared figure is distinctive.
Both use புன்கோட்டி: 255 has the low talking in such assemblies, 260 shows how one is formed when the base man kicks away the learned's teaching (நெஞ்சு உதைத்தலால்) and finds his like.
161's பொறுப்பர் என்று எண்ணி with the faultless great and 700's பழையம் எனக்கருதி with the king share the same logic of presuming on indulgence and coming to ruin, in different domains.
The same claim with different measures: 782's waxing and waning moon (பிறைமதி) and 166's morning shadow shrinking (நாணிழல் ... விளியும்) and evening shadow lengthening.
423 says see the truth whoever speaks (யார்யார்வாய்க் கேட்பினும்); 136 says take good teaching from the learned whatever their caste, as one uses a low-born ferryman. Same claim.
284's crowds who gather like crows while wealth lasts and 231's friends who stay till தங்கரும் முற்றும் show the same self-interested attachment.
168 concludes கலவாமை கோடி உறும் because of the pain of parting, while 174 says no one would resent birth if they could keep நண்பு with the good; the remedies are opposed.
452's நிலத்தியல்பால் நீர்திரிந் தற்றாகும் and 139's new pot giving water the pathiri flower's scent both make understanding take on the nature of one's company.
601 says the lamp of குடி dies when மடி covers it; 199 says birth in உயர்குடி is worth nothing without பேராண்மை. Both say lineage fails without personal energy.
links.text_issue: 199 line 1 reads உளையலா஢ for உளையலரி (an encoding corruption).

links.reason: Both use the eclipse snake and the moon (ஒருபுடை பாம்பு கொளினும் / இளம்பிறை ... சேராது ... அரா), each for a different virtue of the noble; a distinctive shared figure.
251's நுண்ணுணர்வின்மை வறுமை is 841's அறிவின்மை இன்மையுள் இன்மை; the note's additions for each verse are accurate.

72 says bearing the improper words of நேரல்லார் is fitting and the world counts retaliation as சமழ்மை; 117 says இகழ்வாரை முன்னிகழ்க. Opposed counsel for the same situation; the note names the condition.
788 says friendship clears distress at once (ஆங்கே இடுக்கண் களைவது); 369 says one whose heart doesn't ease a friend's நோய் would do better to leap from a cliff.
374's திருவேறு தெள்ளியராதலும் வேறு and 264's புண்ணியமோ வேறே, with the senseless clad in silk while the wise are there, make the same split between wealth and wisdom.

calibration.reason: 471 ends in தூக்கிச் செயல் (weigh, then act); 485's காலம் கருதி இருப்பர் adds timing, and Parimelazhagar says explicitly தம் வலி மிகுமாயினும் அது கருதாது, so a favourable weighing is not enough on its own. The note credits the commentator correctly.

Both make அரண் a matter of the mind: 421's உள்ளழிக்கலாகா அரண் and 534's அச்சமுடையார்க்கு அரணில்லை. But 534's fortress is only the simile for its real point, heedlessness (பொச்சாப்பு). The note's 'fortress is finally a state of mind' overstates it.

34 defines virtue as மனத்துக்கண் மாசிலன் ஆதல, and 455 says how mental purity comes about (இனந்தூய்மை தூவா வரும்). A definition and a cause are compatible, and the note itself describes a deepening rather than an incompatible claim.

753's பொய்யா விளக்கம் means a lamp that never fails to serve. Parimelazhagar says it is so because wealth is always indispensable (எஞ்ஞான்றும் இன்றியமையாததாய்), not because it stays. It does not contradict 333's அற்கா இயல்பிற்று. The tension stretches பொய்யா into 'permanent'.

Manakkudavar on 9 does say உயிருண்டாகில் வணங்கும், so the unbowed head belongs to a body without life, matching 80's என்புதோல் போர்த்த உடம்பு for those without love. The same 'body without the vital quality' logic applies to worship and to love. 'Compete' is a little strong, since both can hold.
232 places புகழ் on those who give to இரப்பார்; 1059 adds that without askers givers would have no தோற்றம். That is an extension, as the note itself describes it, not the same claim.

The link rests on the shared word பேதைமை, but 805's பேதைமை is an occasional lapse in a proven friend (Parimelazhagar: fate-driven folly everyone has), while 797's பேதையார் are fools by nature whom one should not keep. These are different situations, not incompatible claims.

Parimelazhagar glosses 698's ஒளி as the king's divinity of guarding the world while others sleep, which is 388's own ground (காப்பாற்றும்). 698 is about not slighting a king for youth or kinship and says nothing about divinity being unearned, so the conflict is read into the commentary.

800 (நட்பாராய்தல்) is about dropping unsuitable friends taken on unknowingly (Parimelazhagar); 807 (பழைமை) is about long-standing loving friendship. This is different advice for different situations, and the note concedes it only raises an unsettled boundary rather than a contradiction.

Adjacent chapters காலமறிதல் and இடனறிதல் use the same logic: the crow beats the owl by பகல், and the crocodile wins in நெடும்புனல் but loses out of it. Strength depends on circumstance, along time and along place.

874 praises the one who turns enmity into friendship (பகைநட்பாக் கொண்டொழுகும்), and 679 makes winning over the unallied (ஒட்டாரை ஒட்டிக் கொளல்) more urgent than favours to friends. 679 applies 874's quality to a question of timing. Parimelazhagar reads ஒட்டார் as those who are not with one's enemy, which slightly narrows the link.

Parimelazhagar does limit 108 to harm done by the same person who had done good (இரண்டும் ஒருவனாற் செய்யப்பட்ட வழி). 152 states it generally: forgetting an excess (இறப்பு) is better than bearing it (மறத்தல் அதனினும் நன்று). The note is accurate.

An exact structural inversion. ஒருமைக்கண் தான் கற்ற கல்வி ... எழுமையும் ஏமாப்புடைத்து (398) set against ஒருமைச் செயலாற்றும் பேதை எழுமையும் ... அழுந்தும் அளறு (835): one life's doing reaches all seven births, for good in 398 and for ill in 835.

280 applies 34 to ascetic dress: மழித்தலும் நீட்டலும் வேண்டா is an instance of 34's பிற ஆகுலநீர, so the develops link is real. But the note goes on to say that 280's உலகம் பழித்தது ஒழித்து makes the inward standard of 34 not all that matters. That is a stretch, since Parimelazhagar's உலகம் is the wise judging conduct, not a rival outward test.

657 prefers கழிநல்குரவு to wealth gained under blame, and 1041 says nothing pains like இன்மை. These are compatible: one ranks poverty above something worse, and the other measures its pain. The note itself argues they fit together. The real relation is that 657 limits 1041's 'nothing is worse', which is not a tension.

971's ஒளி is உள்ள வெறுக்கை, an abundance of spirit or aspiration (Parimelazhagar: ஊக்கமிகுதி). 1064 praises இரவொல்லாச் சால்பு, refusing to beg in destitution. Calling the refusal the extreme form of aspiration joins two different virtues by stretching உள்ளம்.

Both use the paradox of the beloved as both disease and its cure: one look is நோய் and the other மருந்து (1091), and தன்நோய்க்குத் தானே மருந்து (1102). The movement from glance to person is accurately described.
951's இற்பிறந்தார் கண்அல்லது இல்லை இயல்பாக directly opposes 972's பிறப்பொக்கும் எல்லா உயிர்க்கும், and Kalaignar does invert 951 (those with integrity count as well-born). The note is accurate.

Both trade நாண் plus another quality for a token of love-sickness: சாயலும் நாணும் for நோயும் பசலையும், and நாணொடு நல்லாண்மை for மடல். This before/after inventory is a meaningful shared figure, and the contrast between active and passive is fair.

Manakkudavar does gloss தான் அற as அகங்கார மறுதல் (the ego cut away), which matches 346's யான் எனது என்னும் செருக்கு அறுப்பான, and Kalaignar reads it the same way. The note correctly flags that Parimelazhagar's reading weakens the link.

Both use bangles to reveal the separation of the துறைவன், and the image is distinctive. In 1157 the slipping bangles proclaim it (தூற்றாகொல்), and in 1277 the bangles knew before she did (நம்மினும் முன்னம் உணர்ந்த). In Parimelazhagar's reading 1277 is a separation of mind while he is still present, not a departure.

379 asks why those who welcome good fortune grieve at bad, when both come from fate. 38 says doing good daily blocks rebirth (வாழ்நாள் வழியடைக்கும் கல்). Their only common ground is Parimelazhagar's karma frame, and neither extends the other.

300 says nothing at all is better than வாய்மை (இல்லை எனைத்தொன்றும்), while 323 ranks கொல்லாமை first, with பொய்யாமை பின்சார. Parimelazhagar raises exactly this doubt and harmonizes the two, which confirms that the literal tension is real.

The two connect, since the king who acts வெருவந்த and the இகல்வேந்தர் the courtier must keep a distance from are the same situation seen from both sides. But that is not one pattern carried into a different domain, so the type misfits. The note's point about addressing each party separately is interpretive.

The link rests wholly on Parimelazhagar's elopement settings. They are separate chapters and separate scenes: in 1120 the man praises tender feet (நெருஞ்சிப் பழம்), and in 1279 she glances at her feet (அடிநோக்கி). These are not incompatible claims, and 'the compliment had been an excuse' is the marker's invention.
1103 sets sleeping on the beloved's arms against தாமரைக் கண்ணான் உலகு; 1323 sets புலத்தல் against புத்தேள்நாடு, carrying the heaven comparison over to the lovers' quarrel.
201's விழுமியார் அஞ்சுவர் தீவினை and 366's அஞ்சுவது ... அவா are not the same claim; as the note itself says, 366 moves the fear to craving, the source, which is development.

Parimelazhagar glosses 430's எல்லாம் உடையார் by saying wealth is created and kept by அறிவு, and in his gloss on 374 (திரு வேறு தெள்ளியராதலும் வேறு) he raises and answers exactly this objection, so the tension is real on his readings.

537 and 483 share the 'nothing is hard' formula (அரிய ... இல்லை / அருவினை ... உளவோ) with different conditions, but neither extends the other. The note's claim that the repetition shows no single condition suffices is speculation.

Parimelazhagar does read 304's நகை/உவகை as face and heart, parallel to 786's முகநக/அகநக, so a shared distinction exists; but the note's conclusion ('so a smile alone isn't what is at stake') is muddled and the pairing teaches little.

112's ஆக்கம் சிதைவின்றி for the fair man and 178's அஃகாமை செல்வத்திற்கு ... வெஃகாமை both make wealth last on a moral condition. Kural 171 does tie coveting to a lapse from fairness (நடுவின்றி ... வெஃகின்).

222 says கொளல் தீது, taking is bad even if called a good path; 1051 says இரக்க, beg from those fit to be asked, and puts the blame on the refuser. On a plain reading the two judge the same act oppositely. The note admits the standpoints differ, and that is the reading the conflict depends on.

182's புறனழீஇப் பொய்த்து நகை and 824's முகத்தின் இனிய நகாஅ அகத்தின்னா வஞ்சர் both pick out the false smile over hostility. The note accurately describes the shift from a moral verdict to a practical warning.

The construction is the same: prosperity that seems to be and then perishes (ஆவது போலக் கெடும் / உளபோல இல்லாகித் தோன்றாக் கெடும்), with அளவு in both lines (அளவிறந்து / அளவறிந்து). The அளவு wordplay is a light touch, but the structural echo is real.
calibration.text_issue: Kural 479 has a corrupt character in அளவற஧ந்து (for அளவறிந்து).

calibration.reason: 1151's வல்வரவு வாழ்வார்க்குரை warns that she may not live to see his quick return. On Parimelazhagar's reading of 1270 (உள்ளம் உடைந்துக்கக்கால் ... பெறின் என்னாம்), the hero himself fears exactly that on the way back. The note attributes the speakers to the commentators accurately.

The note itself says both give the same rule (தீப்பால ... பிறர்கண் செய்யற்க / இன்னா ... பிறன்கண் செயல்) on different grounds; neither limits or conditions the other, so this is agreement, not qualification.
calibration.text_issue: The Parimelazhagar text shown under 316 is the commentary on 317 (மனத்தான் ஆம் மாணா), not 316.

calibration.reason: Parimelazhagar's gloss on 1170 ends இதனான் வருகின்ற அதிகாரமும் தோற்றுவாய் செய்யப்பட்டது, so the eyes swimming in tears (நீந்தல ... என் கண்) lead directly into 1171's கண்தாம் கலுழ்வ தெவன்.

The moral-versus-fatal contrast is real, but 377 is about enjoying (துய்த்தல்) what was amassed, not about why people are poor, so it is not 'the same fact'; and Parimelazhagar treats tavam as feeding the same fate, which the note doesn't acknowledge.

Parimelazhagar reads 383's துணிவு as ஒன்றனையும் பாராது கடிதில் செய்வது and Manakkudavar as ஆராய்ந்து துணிதல்; 467's எண்ணித் துணிக specifies resolve after deliberation, so it develops 383 and bears on the reading as the note says.
298 says outer purity comes by water, inner by truth (புறள்தூய்மை நீரான் ... அகந்தூய்மை வாய்மையால்); 278 shows the many who bathe with மனத்தது மாசு. The case and the principle agree.
